review_note: Pinned sdga lemma 2673 asserts j_!A_U is a 'good' DG A-module. Stage A expands the context-defined 'good' into exactness and acyclicity preservation of graded tensor plus universal base change. The 'good' predicate itself is defined outside permitted formal statements; this substantive expansion cannot be verified source-first without prohibited context.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-supply-good}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a sheaf of differential graded algebras
on $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
Then $j_!\mathcal{A}_U$ is a good differential graded
$\mathcal{A}$-module.
hold_reason: Expanded definition of 'good' DG module is not independently verifiable from formal statement/notation environments.
proposed_correction: Recover a permitted source definition of 'good' and check tensor/acyclicity/base-change conditions before renewed independent Stage B review.

review_note: Pinned sdga lemma 2804 says arbitrary direct sums and filtered colimits preserve 'good' DG modules. Stage A appends a nontrivial definition of 'good' that cannot be verified from an allowed formal source declaration; the closure assertions agree but the standalone expansion is uncertified.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-good-direct-sum}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a sheaf of differential graded algebras
on $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. An arbitrary
direct sum of good differential graded $\mathcal{A}$-modules
is good. A filtered colimit of good differential graded
$\mathcal{A}$-modules is good.
hold_reason: The standalone assertion includes the same unverified substantive definition of 'good' DG modules.
proposed_correction: Supply a proof-safe formal definition of 'good' and have a different reviewer certify its closure properties.

review_note: Pinned sdga lemma 2819 asserts existence of a good surjective P→M that also surjects on kernels of differentials. Stage A includes 'there exists a homomorphism P→M' in the structured hypotheses, instead of the theorem's existential conclusion, and expands an unverified 'good' predicate.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-good-quotient}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a sheaf of differential graded algebras
on $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. Let $\mathcal{M}$
be a differential graded $\mathcal{A}$-module. There exists a homomorphism
$\mathcal{P} \to \mathcal{M}$ of differential graded $\mathcal{A}$-modules
with the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{P} \to \mathcal{M}$ is surjective,
\item $\Ker(\text{d}_\mathcal{P}) \to \Ker(\text{d}_\mathcal{M})$
is surjective, and
\item $\mathcal{P}$ is good.
\end{enumerate}
hold_reason: Existence of P→M is incorrectly presented as an assumption, and 'good' is expanded from hidden context.
proposed_correction: Move existence and all three properties into the conclusion; verify formal meaning of good separately and independently re-review.

review_note: Pinned sdga lemma 2968 asserts existence of a good DG-module quasi-isomorphic replacement P→M. Stage A puts the existential existence of P→M in the hypotheses rather than the conclusion and appends a context-dependent definition of 'good'.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-resolve}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a sheaf of differential graded algebras
on $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. Let $\mathcal{M}$
be a differential graded $\mathcal{A}$-module. There exists a homomorphism
$\mathcal{P} \to \mathcal{M}$ of differential graded $\mathcal{A}$-modules

\end{enumerate}

proposed_correction: Use only site, DG algebra and M as hypotheses; assert existence of a good P quasi-isomorphic to M as the conclusion after independent definition review.

review_note: Pinned sdga lemma 3227 gives two consequences of a good acyclic right DG A-module: tensor with any left DG module is acyclic, and compatible ringed-topos pullback is good and acyclic. Stage A expands 'good' via non-formal context and that definition is not available for independent safe source review.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-acyclic-good}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a sheaf of differential graded algebras
on $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a good
acyclic right differential graded $\mathcal{A}$-module.
\begin{enumerate}
\item for any differential graded left $\mathcal{A}$-module
$\mathcal{N}$ the tensor product
$\mathcal{P} \otimes_\mathcal{A} \mathcal{N}$ is acyclic,
\item for any morphism $(f, f^\sharp) : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}')
\to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O})$
of ringed topoi and any differential graded $\mathcal{O}'$-algebra
$\mathcal{A}'$ and any map $\varphi : f^{-1}\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{A}'$
of differential graded $f^{-1}\mathcal{O}$-algebras
the pullback $f^*\mathcal{P}$ is acyclic and good.
\end{enumerate}
hold_reason: Stage A's explicit 'good' predicate is unverified in permitted safe source context.
proposed_correction: Recover a formal definition of good DG modules and independently recheck the two conclusions with their universal quantifiers.
